data.name: Felicianus
data.gender_notes: Felicianus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word ‘felix’, meaning ‘happy’ or ‘fortunate’. In Christianity, the name Felicianus is associated with the early Christian saint Felician, who is the patron saint of young people and animals. The name Felicianus carries the meaning “Man of happiness, fortunate” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Felicianus usually hope their child will grow to embody man of happiness, fortunate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes joy and prosperity in life, often reflecting one's positive outlook and optimistic attitude.
data.etymology: Felicianus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man of happiness, fortunate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Felicianus total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_greek.name: Φηλικιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Φηλικιανός είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό 'Felicianus', που σημαίνει χαρά ή ευτυχία. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό στην πρώιμη χριστιανική εκκλησία και φέρει βαθιά πνευματική σημασία χαράς και ευλογίας.

data.cultural_impact: The name Felicianus holds a rich cultural heritage as it is derived from the Latin word felix, which means 'happy' or 'fortunate'. This name has been popular in various Christian communities due to its association with St. Felician, an early Christian martyr and patron saint, who was known for his happiness and good fortune despite persecution and suffering.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Felicianus carries a profound spiritual significance as it symbolizes joy, hope, and faith in the face of adversity. The name Felicianus serves as a reminder of the inner strength and resilience that St. Felician exemplified, inspiring those bearing the name to remain steadfast and joyful in their own spiritual journeys. This name also speaks to the blessings and grace that come from God, giving praise to the divine source of all happiness and fortune.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Felicianus, derived from the Latin word "felix," meaning happy or fortunate, embodies the hope and joy found in the Christian faith. This name symbolizes the belief that God bestows blessings upon His people and that all Christians, through faith and trust, can lead a joyful and fulfilling life.

historical_references.reference: Saint Felicianus was a bishop of Córdoba during the Roman period. He is said to have been martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian in 304 AD.

Saint Felicianus was also a bishop of Narni in Italy during the early Christian period. He is believed to have been a disciple of Saint Peter and was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Nero in 64 AD.
